Rashi on Temurah 6a:10:1.hebrew: מעשר - תחילה, ואח"כ נותן (לה) פאה:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:10:1.english: He tithes - First, and afterward he gives pe’a.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:10:2.hebrew: תיובתא דאביי - דאמר מהני, דהא הכא לא מהני:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:10:2.english: A conclusive refutation of Abaye - For he said that it is effective [when the owner harvests the grain], yet here [in this baraita] it is not effective.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:11:1.hebrew: תעזוב תעזוב - תרי זימני כתיב "לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם": חד ב"קדושים תהיו", וחד ב"אמור אל הכהנים". ולמה כפלו? לאשמועינן מקרא דתעזוב יתירא, דאע"ג דאישתני בידו, לא קנייה:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:11:1.english: "You shall leave," "You shall leave" - It is written twice, "for the poor and for the stranger you shall leave them": once in Kedoshim Tihyu and once in Emor el HaKohanim. Why was it repeated? To teach us, from the superfluous verse of "you shall leave," that even though it changed in his possession (i.e., he harvested it and kneaded it into dough), he has not acquired it.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:13:1.hebrew: חייב בפרט ובעוללות כו' - ואע"ג דהפקר פטור מכל אלו, הפקר כי האי חייב, דנפקא לן מ"תעזוב" יתירא, דבכולהו כתיב "תעזוב" יתירא:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:13:1.english: He is obligated in peret and in olelot, etc. - And although ownerless property is exempt from all of these, ownerless property like this one is obligated, for we derive it from the superfluous "you shall leave [them]" (ta'azov), since in all of them the superfluous "you shall leave" is written:

Rashi on Temurah 6a:13:2.hebrew: ופטור מן המעשר - דבמעשר לא כתיב "תעזוב" יתירא. ולרבויי האי הפקר אתא "תעזוב", ולא לרבויי שינוי, דהא בעלמא נמי לא מהני:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:13:2.english: And he is exempt from tithes - For regarding tithes, the superfluous [word] "you shall leave" is not written. And "you shall leave" comes to include this case of ownerless property [that was later reclaimed], and not to include [a change of status through] a change [of the produce's form], since in general, too, [such a change] is not effective.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:14:1.hebrew: והשתא דמשנינן כל הני שינויי - דאיכא דמהני, ואיכא דלא מהני, ובכולהו מודו אביי ורבא — אם כן, במאי פליגי:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:14:1.english: And now that we have answered all these answers - That there are [cases] where it is effective and there are [cases] where it is not effective, and in all of them Abaye and Rava agree — [if so,] in what do they disagree?

Rashi on Temurah 6a:1:1.hebrew: נדבה תעשה אותו - ואמרינן לקמן (תמורה דף ז:) אלו קדשי בדק הבית. ואיכא למשמע מ״אותו״: אתה מתפיס לבדק הבית, ואי אתה מתפיס תמימין לבדק הבית:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:1:1.english: “A gift you may offer it” - And we say later (Temurah 7b): “These” are consecrated items for Temple maintenance. And one can derive from “it” that you may consecrate [a blemished animal] for Temple maintenance, but you may not consecrate unblemished animals for Temple maintenance.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:1:2.hebrew: בלא תעשה - כדדרשינן לקמן: וידבר ה' אל משה לאמר — לא אמור:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:1:2.english: A negative commandment - As we expound below: “And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying [lemor]” — read it as lo emor (“not, say”), meaning that a negative commandment is stated.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:2:1.hebrew: מהיכא דאיתרבו בעלי מומין למזבח - מהמקום שבו נתרבו בעלי מומים למזבח, שהם דקדשי בדיעבד:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:2:1.english: From where blemished animals were included for the altar - [From the source that teaches] that they are consecrated after the fact.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:2:2.hebrew: איתרבו כו' - דהא בההוא קרא כתיב "ולנדר לא ירצה", ואמרינן לקמן (תמורה דף ז:) אלו קדשי מזבח. וכתיב "לא ירצה", דמשמע רצויי לא מרצו, הא מקדש קדשי. ואיתקוש תמימין לבדק הבית לבעלי מומין למזבח, דהא מחד קרא נפקי לאיסורא דלא מקדיש. הלכך איתקוש נמי לענין דיעבד מה שעשה עשוי:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:2:2.english: They are included, etc. - For in that very verse it is written, "and for a vow it shall not be accepted," and we say below (Temurah 7b) that these are animals consecrated for the altar. And it is written "it shall not be accepted," which implies that they are not accepted for sacrifice, but nevertheless they do become consecrated. And unblemished animals for Temple maintenance were compared to blemished animals for the altar, since both are derived from one verse as to the prohibition, that one may not consecrate them. Therefore, they were also compared with regard to the after-the-fact law that what was done is done.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:3:1.hebrew: כשעת הגזילה - משלם דמי צמר ועצים בעלמא, אבל הכלים והבגדים קנה בשינוי. אלמא מהני שינוי לקנות:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:3:1.english: According to the time of the robbery - [He pays the value of] the plain wool and wood only, but the vessels and garments he acquired through the change. Evidently, [a change] is effective [to acquire the item]:

Rashi on Temurah 6a:4:1.hebrew: אשר גזל כעין שגזל - את הגזילה יחזיר:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:4:1.english: "That which he took by robbery" — like that which he robbed - He shall return the stolen item.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:5:1.hebrew: ואביי - להכי לא איצטריך, הפסוק דאנא ידענא דמהני שבועה והודאה. אלא להך דרשא: דהאי "אשר גזל" כתיב גבי שבועה שנשבע לשקר, וכתיב (ויקרא ה) "יוסיף חומש". וקמ"ל דעל גזילו מוסיף חומש, אם נשבע לשקר והודה:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:5:1.english: And Abaye - It is not needed for this purpose, for I already know that an oath and subsequent admission are effective. Rather, it is needed for this exposition: that this phrase "that he robbed" is written with regard to an oath that one swore falsely, and it is written (Leviticus 5) "he shall add a fifth." And it teaches us that for his own robbery he adds a fifth, if he swore falsely and then admitted.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:5:2.english: And he does not add a fifth for the robbery of his father - Even if he swore falsely concerning it.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:6:1.hebrew: מחזיר את הכר בלילה כו' - וגבי ממשכנין בעל כרחו קתני לה, בבבא מציעא בפ' המקבל (בבא מציעא דף קיג.). אלמא מהני וקני למשכון יום — דהיינו מחרישה — קני המלוה בלילה, וכסות לילה קני מלוה ביום. אלמא מהני:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:6:1.english: He returns the mattress at night, etc. - And it is regarding [a creditor who] seizes collateral against the debtor's will that it teaches this, in Bava Metzia, in the chapter [entitled] HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 113a). Evidently, [the seizure] is effective, and the creditor acquires the collateral of the day — that is, the plow — [and keeps it] at night; and [the creditor] acquires the garment needed at night [and keeps it] by day. Evidently, it is effective.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:7:1.hebrew: שאני התם דכתיב השב תשיבנו לו - מריבויא דקרא נפקא לן דמחזיר כמה פעמים, ולא משכחת לה אלא הכי: דמחזיר כלי יום ביום, וכלי לילה בלילה. ומהכא נפקא לן דקני. ולאביי ריבויא דקרא לא משמע ליה, והשב תשיבנו איצטריך, דאי לא כתיב ביה הוה אמינא איבעי ניהדר איבעי לא ניהדר:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:7:1.english: It is different there, as it is written: "You shall surely restore it to him" - From the amplification of the verse (the doubled verb) we derive that he returns [the pledge] many times. And this can be accomplished only in this way: that he returns a utensil [used by] day during the day, and a utensil [used by] night at night. And from here we derive that [the creditor] acquires [a lien on the pledge]. But according to Abaye, the amplification of the verse does not imply this to him, and "you shall surely restore it" was needed because, had it not been written there, I would have said: if he wishes, let him return it; if he wishes, let him not return it.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:7:2.hebrew: ה"ג ל"א אמר לך רבא שאני התם דכתיב עד בא השמש תשיבנו - ודרשינן ליה בהמקבל הכי: כל היום עד שיבא השמש תשיבנו ללוה, ובבוא השמש תקחנו ממנו — מכאן לכסות יום שניתנה ליחבל בלילה. וכתיב קרא אחרינא: השב תשיבנו כבוא השמש — מכאן לכסות לילה שניתנה ליחבל ביום. ומהכא נפקא לן דמהני. ואביי אמר לך: לאו לאשמועינן דמהני, אלא חד לכסות יום שיחזירנו ביום, וחד לכסות לילה שחייב להחזירו בלילה, וצריכי. והאי וצריכי לא איתפרש לן, ונראה לי דהכי הוא: דאי אשמעינן לכסות יום, כגון מחרישה, משום דחיותיה הוא; אבל כסות לילה, אימא לא. ואי כתיב כסות לילה, משום דמצטער; אבל כסות יום, אימא לא:
Rashi on Temurah 6a:7:2.english: Thus we read; another version: Rava said to you: It is different there, as it is written: "Until the sun sets, you shall return it to him" - And we expound it in [the chapter] Hamekabel as follows: All day, until the sun sets, you shall return it to the debtor, and when the sun sets, you shall take it from him — from here [we learn the law of] a day garment that was given as a pledge to be taken at night. And another verse is written: "You shall surely return it to him when the sun sets" — from here [we learn the law of] a night garment that was given as a pledge to be taken by day. And from here we derive that [the transgression of taking it] is effective. And Abaye could say to you: [The verses are] not to teach us that it is effective; rather, one is for a day garment, that he must return it by day, and one is for a night garment, that he is obligated to return it at night, and both are needed. But this "both are needed" was not explained to us, and it seems to me that it is as follows: If [the Torah] had taught us only about a day garment, such as a plow, [one might think this is] because it is his livelihood; but a night garment, I would say no. And if it had written only a night garment, [one might think this is] because he suffers; but a day garment, I would say no.

Rashi on Temurah 6a:9:1.english: Smoothed it - For it has become fixed for tithes and for teruma.

Tosafot on Temurah 6a:10:1.hebrew: אף מפריש מן העיסה - ואין שינוי שם קונה:
Tosafot on Temurah 6a:10:1.english: He separates even from the dough - And a change of name does not acquire [i.e., it does not make the produce the owner's property, so the poor person's right to pe'a remains]:

Tosafot on Temurah 6a:13:1.hebrew: המפקיר כרמו והשכים לבקר ובצרו חייב בפרט ובעוללות ובשכחה ופאה - פירש"י: אע"ג דהפקר פטור מכל אלו, הפקר כי האי חייב, ונפקא לן מ"תעזוב" יתירא, דבכולהו כתיב "תעזוב" יתירא. ואור"י דהחיוב תלוי היכא דזכה בגוף השדה, אבל היכא דלא זכה רק בפירות — פטור מכולהו:
Tosafot on Temurah 6a:13:1.english: "One who renounces ownership of his vineyard, and rises early in the morning and harvests it, is obligated in peret, olelot, forgotten sheaves [shikhecha], and pe'a" - Rashi explained: Even though ownerless property is exempt from all of these, ownerless property of this kind is obligated, and we derive this from the superfluous "you shall leave [them]" (ta'azov), as with regard to all of them the word "you shall leave" is written superfluously. And the Rabbi [Rabbeinu Yitzchak, the Ri] said: The obligation depends on the case where he acquired the body of the field itself, but where he acquired only the produce, he is exempt from all of them.

Tosafot on Temurah 6a:14:1.hebrew: והשתא דשנינן כל הני שינויי אביי ורבא במאי פליגי - וא"ת: נימא דפליגי בהכי, כגון אדם שנשבע שלא לגרש את אשתו, ואחר כך עבר וגירשה, דלאביי מהני, ולרבא לא מהני גירושין כיון דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא? ויש לומר: כיון שאין האיסור כמו "לא יוכל לשלחה", אלא שהוא בדה את האיסור, בכה"ג לא אמר רבא דלא מהני. וקשיא לרבינו ברוך: אמאי לא קאמר דפליגי בהכי, כגון אם פדה בכור או מעשר או חרמים, לא מהני לכ"ע, כדמפרש סוגיא, דלאביי לא לקי כיון דלא מהני, דהכי אמר אביי לעיל דהיכא דלא מהני לא לקי, ולרבא לקי משום דעבר אמימרא דרחמנא? צ"ע:
Tosafot on Temurah 6a:14:1.english: "And now that we have given all of these answers, with regard to what do Abaye and Rava disagree?" - And if you say: Let us say that they disagree about this — for example, a person who swore not to divorce his wife, and afterward transgressed and divorced her, so that according to Abaye the divorce is effective, and according to Rava the divorce is not effective, since he transgressed the statement of the Merciful One? And one can answer: Since the prohibition is not like "he may not send her away" (Deuteronomy 22:19), but rather he himself invented the prohibition, in such a case Rava did not say that it is not effective. But Rabbeinu Barukh found it difficult: Why does it not say that they disagree about this — for example, if one redeemed a firstborn animal, or animal tithe, or consecrated property (ḥaramim), where it is not effective according to everyone, as the passage explains, so that according to Abaye he is not lashed, since it is not effective, for so Abaye said earlier, that where it is not effective one is not lashed, and according to Rava he is lashed because he transgressed the statement of the Merciful One? It requires further study.

Tosafot on Temurah 6a:3:1.english: He pays according to the time of the robbery - because a change [in the item] acquires it. Evidently, [the act] takes effect even though it is done through a transgression, and this is a conclusive refutation of Rava:

Tosafot on Temurah 6a:6:1.hebrew: מחזיר את הכר בלילה ואת המחרישה ביום ותיובתא דרבא - דאי לא מהני לא היה תפיסתו תפיסה, והיה לו להחזירם לבעלים מכל וכל. ואם תאמר: מנלן דהא מתניתין במשכנו שלא ברשות איירי? דלמא במשכנו שליח בית דין קאמר דמחזיר הכר בלילה והמחרישה ביום, דלא עבר; אבל היכא דעבר אימא לך דלא מהני. וי"ל דהך משנה מיתניא בפרק המקבל (ב"מ דף קיג.) גבי משכנו שלא ברשות, דתני לעיל מיניה: המלוה חבירו לא ימשכנו אלא בבית דין, ולא יכנס לביתו ליטול משכונו, שנאמר "בחוץ תעמוד"; היו לו שני כלים נוטל אחד ומניח אחד, מחזיר את הכר בלילה ואת המחרישה ביום. אלמא אשלא ברשות קאי:
Tosafot on Temurah 6a:6:1.english: "He returns the mattress by night and the plow by day" — and this is a refutation of Rava - For if [seizing collateral without authorization] were not effective, his seizure would not be a valid seizure, and he would have had to return the items to their owners entirely. And if you say: How do we know that this mishna is speaking about one who seized collateral without authorization? Perhaps it is speaking of one who seized collateral through an agent of the court, and it says that he returns the mattress by night and the plow by day because he did not transgress; but where he did transgress, I would say to you that [the seizure] is not effective. And one can answer that this mishna is taught in the chapter [entitled] HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 113a), regarding one who seized collateral without authorization, for it teaches just before it: One who lends to another may not seize collateral from him except through a court, and he may not enter his house to take his pledge, as it is stated: "You shall stand outside" (Deuteronomy 24:11). If [the debtor] had two items, [the creditor] takes one and leaves one; he returns the mattress by night and the plow by day. Evidently it is speaking of [seizure] without authorization:
